fto2q.q: Penalties apply to anyone who, even while wearing the seatbelt, tampers with it or obstructs its normal operation.
fto2q.why: Tampering with a seatbelt or blocking its normal operation is punishable, even if you are wearing it.

1jes504.q: If you do not fasten the seatbelt, in a sudden braking you can be thrown against the windscreen.
1jes504.why: Without a belt your body keeps moving forward through inertia and can hit the windscreen (parabrezza) in hard braking.

ljmd8y.q: If the vehicle has front and side airbags, you can do without fastening the seatbelt.
ljmd8y.why: Airbags only supplement the seatbelt, never replace it: the belt must always be fastened.

16ws5u3.q: Seatbelts must be fastened only when driving at a speed of 30 km/h or more.
16ws5u3.why: The obligation applies at any speed; there is no minimum speed threshold.

1dasoor.q: In vehicles with an airbag fitted with a disabling control, before placing a child seat (backrest facing the windscreen) on the front seat, the airbag must be deactivated.
1dasoor.why: A rear-facing child seat in front needs the passenger airbag switched off, otherwise its deployment could seriously injure the child.

peksfx.q: In vehicles without a control to disable the passenger-side airbag, a child seat must not be placed on the front seat with its backrest facing the road.
peksfx.why: If the passenger airbag cannot be disabled, a rear-facing child seat must not go on the front seat.

b4kxg5.q: If a vehicle is fitted with an airbag, there is no obligation to wear seatbelts while driving.
b4kxg5.why: Seatbelts remain compulsory; the airbag is designed to work together with the belt, not instead of it.

10lmtrc.q: The headrest is useful to prevent "whiplash".
10lmtrc.why: The headrest (poggiatesta) limits backward head movement in a collision, preventing whiplash (colpo di frusta).

1p7ktfh.q: The headrest is useful if it is correctly adjusted, both in height and in angle.
1p7ktfh.why: A headrest only protects when properly adjusted in height and angle, level with the back of the head.

fn510b.q: The headrest is particularly useful for relaxing the muscles while driving.
fn510b.why: The headrest is a safety device against whiplash, not a comfort aid for relaxing muscles.

ldk9td.q: The headrest has an aesthetic function, not a safety one.
ldk9td.why: The headrest is a real safety device that prevents neck injuries (whiplash).

1y0wozt.q: Pregnant women with certified special risk conditions are not required to fasten the seatbelt.
1y0wozt.why: Pregnant women with a certified special risk are exempt from the seatbelt obligation.

12p7wo1.q: People suffering from certain certified illnesses are not required to fasten the seatbelt.
12p7wo1.why: People with certified medical conditions are exempt from wearing the seatbelt.

1j6y0h3.q: Driving instructors, while carrying out their profession, are not obliged to fasten the seatbelt.
1j6y0h3.why: Driving instructors are exempt from the seatbelt obligation while teaching.

hb5vm0.q: The postman, during working activity, is not obliged to fasten the seatbelt.
hb5vm0.why: There is no exemption for postal workers: the seatbelt obligation applies at work too.

t77pox.q: People over 65 years of age are not obliged to fasten the seatbelt.
t77pox.why: Age gives no exemption: seatbelts are compulsory at any age.

10zmr8n.q: Whoever drives a car with a driving practice authorisation (foglio rosa) is not obliged to use the seatbelt.
10zmr8n.why: A learner driver with a foglio rosa must wear the seatbelt like any other driver.

hgcug7.q: Helmets are compulsory for riders of two-wheeled mopeds.
hgcug7.why: An approved helmet is compulsory for riders of two-wheeled mopeds (ciclomotori).

13riiv4.q: Helmets are compulsory for riders of motorcycles not fitted with a safety cell and restraint devices.
13riiv4.why: On motorcycles without a safety cell and restraint systems, the rider must wear a helmet.

gfciid.q: Helmets are compulsory for the passenger of a motorcycle without a safety cell and restraint systems.
gfciid.why: The passenger of a motorcycle without a safety cell must also wear a helmet.

1pzb409.q: Helmets are compulsory for the passenger of a two-wheeled moped, even if an adult.
1pzb409.why: The helmet obligation covers the passenger too, whatever their age.

q962wr.q: Helmets are compulsory for riders of two-wheeled mopeds only if they are minors.
q962wr.why: Helmets are compulsory for all moped riders, adults included.

11yfwoj.q: Helmets are not compulsory for riders of two-wheeled mopeds who hold a category B licence.
11yfwoj.why: Everyone must wear a helmet on a two-wheeled moped, including category B licence holders.

1yeeix2.q: Helmets are not compulsory for riders of two-wheeled mopeds.
1yeeix2.why: Helmets are compulsory for riders of two-wheeled mopeds, with no exceptions.

3ednj0.q: Seatbelts are meant to limit injuries to the driver and passengers in a road accident.
3ednj0.why: Seatbelts hold occupants in their seats and reduce injuries in a crash.

1yps5ov.q: Seatbelts must be worn by both the driver and the passengers of cars that are fitted with them.
1yps5ov.why: Both driver and passengers must wear belts in every seat that has one.

csj8md.q: Seatbelts require periodic checks of their wear and efficiency.
csj8md.why: Seatbelts wear out and need regular checks to make sure they work properly.

1r07da1.q: Seatbelts must be of an approved type and always kept in working order.
1r07da1.why: Seatbelts must be type-approved (omologate) and always kept in good working order.

iezsr9.q: Seatbelts are meant to keep the body attached to the seat in a violent impact.
iezsr9.why: The belt holds your body against the seat in a violent collision.

od5ke4.q: Seatbelts are meant to prevent the driver or passengers from hitting the vehicle's interior parts in a violent impact.
od5ke4.why: The belt stops occupants from striking the steering wheel, dashboard or windscreen in a violent crash.

1aemzgz.q: Seatbelts are meant to prevent the driver or passengers from being thrown out of the car in a violent impact.
1aemzgz.why: The belt keeps occupants from being ejected from the car in a violent crash.

3me7t0.q: Seatbelts must be used in any driving situation.
3me7t0.why: The obligation always applies, regardless of speed, distance or type of road.

o2nwtn.q: Seatbelts must also be used by passengers on the rear seats of cars.
o2nwtn.why: The obligation includes rear seats that are fitted with belts.

1mhf095.q: Seatbelts must be of an approved type and always kept in working order.
1mhf095.why: Seatbelts must be type-approved (omologate) and always kept in good working order.

bwvl85.q: It is not compulsory to use seatbelts in a car when travelling below 30 km/h.
bwvl85.why: There is no minimum speed: the seatbelt must always be fastened.

avuxqm.q: It is not compulsory, but recommended, to wear seatbelts if you occupy the rear seats of a car.
avuxqm.why: On rear seats fitted with belts, wearing them is compulsory, not just advisable.

11u2a3.q: It is not compulsory to use seatbelts in a car for elderly people (over 70 years of age).
11u2a3.why: Age does not exempt anyone: seatbelts are compulsory for everybody.

8wqsgg.q: It is not compulsory to use seatbelts on vehicles fitted with an air-bag.
8wqsgg.why: An airbag never replaces the seatbelt, which remains compulsory.

tk9bb2.q: The warning light indicating unfastened belts can be disabled by the driver with a control on the dashboard.
tk9bb2.why: The unfastened-belt warning light cannot be disabled by the driver.

jbb2j7.q: Obese people may use special devices that keep the seatbelt from lying close to the body.
jbb2j7.why: Devices that stop the belt fitting snugly against the body are forbidden; obesity is not an exemption.

o1m9p7.q: The seatbelt retractor can be deactivated or modified by the driver if it bothers the passenger.
o1m9p7.why: The retractor (arrotolatore) must not be deactivated or modified; doing so is prohibited and fined.

98vo2k.q: Seatbelts are of negligible usefulness in urban traffic.
98vo2k.why: Even at low urban speeds the belt prevents serious injuries, and it is always compulsory.

1x2az4l.q: It is not compulsory to use seatbelts in a car on journeys shorter than one kilometre within built-up areas.
1x2az4l.why: There is no exemption for short trips or built-up areas (centri abitati): belts are always compulsory.

psjhpc.q: Using seatbelts makes it possible to carry children on the front seats in an adult's arms, without danger.
psjhpc.why: Children must never be held in an adult's arms; they need a proper child restraint, and the adult's belt does not protect them.

1ug4ztj.q: Children under 3 years of age cannot travel in cars lacking suitable restraint systems.
1ug4ztj.why: Children under 3 may not travel in a car without a suitable restraint system.

1j6jiz6.q: If a car is fitted with an airbag, children can be carried on the front seat secured in a suitable child seat only if the vehicle has a control to deactivate the airbag.
1j6jiz6.why: A rear-facing child seat in front is allowed only if the airbag can be, and is, switched off.

qhgk92.q: Child restraint systems must be of an approved type and always kept in working order.
qhgk92.why: Child restraint systems must be type-approved (omologati) and always kept in good working order.

1b4hmv7.q: Child restraint systems are of a single type and can all be used to carry children up to 1.50 metres in height.
1b4hmv7.why: There are several types of restraint, chosen according to the child's weight and height.

1b6ahft.q: Carrying children without securing them in restraint systems is allowed, provided it is on urban routes.
1b6ahft.why: Children under 1.50 m must always be secured in a restraint system, even in town.

1cprtzf.q: Carrying children without securing them in restraint systems is allowed, provided the maximum speed is 40 km/h.
1cprtzf.why: No speed is low enough to skip the child restraint system.

3hcf3b.q: Carrying children without securing them in restraint systems is allowed, provided they are on the front seats within the driver's reach.
3hcf3b.why: Being within the driver's reach does not replace the restraint system, which is always required.

zjrr3c.q: Carrying children without securing them in restraint systems is allowed, provided they are on the front seats in the arms of an adult.
zjrr3c.why: Holding a child in your arms is forbidden: a proper restraint system is always required.

16jhisl.q: Seatbelts can be used instead of restraint systems to carry a child, provided the child is taller than 1.30 metres.
16jhisl.why: The seatbelt alone is enough only from 1.50 m in height; below that a child restraint is needed.

1nb8kmp.q: Child seats may also be home-made, provided they are approved by an ASL expert.
1nb8kmp.why: Child seats must be type-approved (omologati); an ASL expert's approval is not enough.

e8sq1t.q: The airbag is an inflatable cushion made of nylon or another synthetic material.
e8sq1t.why: An airbag is an inflatable cushion made of nylon or another synthetic material.

tzgaku.q: The airbag activates in a road accident with a violent impact.
tzgaku.why: The airbag deploys in violent impacts, when sensors detect sharp deceleration.

1vz5r1z.q: The airbag can be dangerous if it deploys while the seatbelt is not worn.
1vz5r1z.why: Without a belt the occupant is out of position, and the airbag's violent inflation can cause serious injury.

1lubelt.q: The airbag serves to limit injuries to vehicle occupants from hitting interior surfaces in a violent impact following an accident.
1lubelt.why: The airbag cushions occupants against the vehicle's interior surfaces in a violent crash.

t65kwi.q: The airbag can sometimes be deactivated.
t65kwi.why: Some vehicles have a control to switch off the passenger airbag, for example when fitting a child seat.

1prpice.q: The airbag inflates automatically on the command of a sensor.
1prpice.why: A sensor detects the impact and triggers inflation automatically.

t5mvcc.q: The airbag inflates in a few milliseconds.
t5mvcc.why: Inflation takes only a few thousandths of a second, so it protects the occupant in time.

13cipc3.q: The airbag inflates in a few seconds.
13cipc3.why: It inflates in milliseconds, not seconds; it must act within the instant of the impact.

14lhyr8.q: The airbag inflates by pressing a button on the dashboard.
14lhyr8.why: Inflation is automatic, triggered by a sensor, not by a button.

rna8q9.q: The airbag must be inflated periodically to check its efficiency.
rna8q9.why: An airbag is never test-inflated; it deploys only once, in a crash.

fjql31.q: The airbag is useful only on extra-urban routes.
fjql31.why: The airbag protects in any violent crash, in town or out of town.

1q7pbkx.q: The airbag must not be used together with seatbelts.
1q7pbkx.why: Airbag and seatbelt must be used together; the airbag is a complementary system.

1ojazc6.q: The airbag cannot be fitted on cars with fewer than 4 doors.
1ojazc6.why: There is no limit linked to the number of doors; an airbag can be fitted to any car.

x9ps78.q: The driver cannot adjust, with a control, the minimum impact speed at which the airbag deploys
x9ps78.why: The airbag deploys based on the vehicle's sensors and control unit. The driver has no control to set its trigger threshold.

8cuo3g.q: The helmet ages because of light and heat
8cuo3g.why: Light and heat degrade the helmet's materials, so its protective ability decreases over time.

1vjbiu2.q: The helmet must be cleaned with non-corrosive detergents
1vjbiu2.why: A helmet should be cleaned with water and mild, non-corrosive detergents, which do not damage the shell or padding.

jobt0m.q: The helmet must not be cleaned with solvents
jobt0m.why: Solvents can attack the shell and inner materials and reduce the protection the helmet provides.

10r7wfr.q: The helmet must not be cleaned with petrol
10r7wfr.why: Petrol is a solvent that can weaken the helmet's shell and materials.

155me6j.q: Wearing a helmet is necessary to reduce the effects of any impacts to the head
155me6j.why: The helmet absorbs impact energy and reduces head injuries in a fall or crash.

1tdkmdg.q: The full-face helmet also protects the face from trauma and injuries in an accident
1tdkmdg.why: The full-face helmet (casco integrale) has a chin guard, so it protects the face and chin as well as the head.

1xx6iah.q: It is good for the helmet to have a visor
1xx6iah.why: A visor protects the eyes and face from wind, rain, dust and insects, making riding safer.

34b72y.q: The helmet visor protects the face and eyes from impacts with insects
34b72y.why: The visor acts as a barrier in front of the face and eyes, stopping insects and debris from hitting them.

1bce8ff.q: The helmet must be the correct size
1bce8ff.why: A helmet of the wrong size does not stay firmly in place and does not protect effectively in an impact.

1c1toap.q: The helmet must be replaced after it has suffered a hard impact, even if the outer shell shows no deformation
1c1toap.why: After a hard impact the inner structure may be damaged even with no visible marks on the shell, so the helmet must be replaced.

j319ac.q: The strength of the helmet's outer shell could be compromised by solvents present in paints or glues
j319ac.why: Solvents in paints or glues can weaken the shell material and reduce its strength.

f8l38v.q: While riding, the helmet must always be properly fastened
f8l38v.why: The helmet must always be fastened properly with the chin strap (sottogola), otherwise it can come off in a fall.

n3rs3l.q: Wearing the helmet incorrectly or without fastening it properly can cause serious health risks in a fall or accident
n3rs3l.why: A badly worn or unfastened helmet can come off on impact and leave the head unprotected.

zezcvb.q: The helmet must be worn even for short trips and at low speed
zezcvb.why: The helmet requirement always applies, with no exception for short trips or low speed; even a slow fall can cause serious injury.

yn39cq.q: The helmet must also be worn on motorised quadricycles without bodywork (quads)
yn39cq.why: On motorised quadricycles without bodywork (quads) the helmet is compulsory, as on motorcycles.

1ul1wfn.q: The helmet visor must be replaced if scratched or damaged
1ul1wfn.why: A scratched or damaged visor reduces visibility and may break dangerously, so it must be replaced.

1895wzb.q: The helmet visor must guarantee perfect vision in any light conditions
1895wzb.why: The visor must be clear and not distort vision, whatever the lighting conditions.

15g4vbm.q: The helmet's ventilation system helps limit the risk of the visor fogging up
15g4vbm.why: The helmet's air vents let air circulate and reduce fogging of the visor.

18xw7h8.q: A driver who does not wear a helmet is subject to deduction of points from the driving licence
18xw7h8.why: Riding without a helmet is an offence punished also by deduction of points (decurtazione di punti) from the licence.

tj25p6.q: Stickers of any kind may be applied to the helmet, as long as they do not cover the visor
tj25p6.why: Stickers contain glues and solvents that can damage the shell, so stickers of any kind must not be applied.

kashv2.q: The helmet must be cleaned periodically with petrol or turpentine to degrease it and remove insect remains
kashv2.why: Petrol and turpentine are solvents that damage the helmet. It should be cleaned with water and mild detergent.

1hflzez.q: The helmet must be fully fastened only on out-of-town roads
1hflzez.why: The helmet must be fastened on every type of road, urban or out-of-town.

5fuy5s.q: When riding in controlled-speed zones below 30 km/h, wearing a helmet is not compulsory
5fuy5s.why: The helmet is compulsory in low-speed zones too, such as 30 km/h zones.

73od5m.q: Wearing a helmet is compulsory on any motorised quadricycle
73od5m.why: The helmet is compulsory only on quadricycles without bodywork (quads); it is not required on those with bodywork.

1em9au.q: The helmet keeps its protective characteristics unchanged for very long periods, over twenty years
1em9au.why: Helmet materials age and lose effectiveness over time, so a helmet must be replaced after a few years, not twenty.

9k7v2a.q: The full-face helmet cannot be used when riding in busy urban areas
9k7v2a.why: The full-face helmet can be used anywhere, including in cities; it is in fact the most protective type.

2x52mk.q: The full-face helmet is useless when riding a two-wheeled moped
2x52mk.why: The full-face helmet is useful on a moped too, because it protects head and face in a fall.

14ojx32.q: The helmet requirement does not apply to adults with more than three years of driving experience
14ojx32.why: The helmet requirement applies to all riders and passengers, regardless of age or driving experience.

j94fm0.q: Wearing the helmet while riding becomes optional when the air temperature is above thirty degrees
j94fm0.why: The helmet is compulsory at all times, whatever the temperature.

k8b8tz.q: The helmet visor greatly worsens visibility and should therefore be used as little as possible
k8b8tz.why: The visor protects against wind, rain and insects and, when clean, does not worsen visibility, so it should be used normally.

wr9fp6.q: The helmet shell may be repaired with special adhesive tape if the break is less than three centimetres
wr9fp6.why: A damaged shell cannot be repaired, even with special tape; the helmet must be replaced.

1q8tpvj.q: The helmet visor may be repaired with adhesive tape, as long as it is ultra-transparent
1q8tpvj.why: A damaged visor must not be repaired with tape, which impairs its clarity; it must be replaced.

v76tl4.q: Helmets for riding mopeds do not need type approval
v76tl4.why: Helmets for mopeds must also be type-approved (omologati), meaning they meet safety standards.

kmfzf8.q: Motorcycle boots provide proper protection for the feet and ankles when riding a two-wheeled vehicle
kmfzf8.why: Motorcycle boots protect the feet and ankles in a fall or impact.

8zs19j.q: Motorcycle boots reduce the effects of sprains from imprecise foot placement and protect the ankle joints from the cold
8zs19j.why: Motorcycle boots support the ankle, limiting sprains, and shield it from the cold.

25276h.q: Motorcycle boots have no loose straps or laces, to prevent them catching on the motorcycle's pedals
25276h.why: Motorcycle boots have no loose laces, which could catch on the pedals or controls.

1ow9ke8.q: Motorcycle boots protect the feet from abrasion on the asphalt in a fall
1ow9ke8.why: The tough material of motorcycle boots protects the foot from sliding along the asphalt.

dmm8hv.q: Motorcycle boots are type-approved according to international standards
dmm8hv.why: Motorcycle boots are type-approved (omologati) to international safety standards.

98u5y2.q: Footwear approved for motorcycle use is designed not to come off in a fall
98u5y2.why: Approved motorcycle footwear is designed to stay on the feet even in a fall.

9u4cka.q: High-mountain trekking shoes can be used instead of motorcycle boots, because they are of similar design
9u4cka.why: Trekking shoes are designed differently and do not protect in a motorcycle fall, so they are not a substitute.

dgdd24.q: Motorcycle boots have double laces to prevent them coming off
dgdd24.why: Motorcycle boots do not use double laces; they are designed without loose laces and with secure fastenings.

mcquor.q: Motorcycle boots have a steel sole
mcquor.why: Motorcycle boots have hard-wearing non-slip soles, not steel ones.

zpcaka.q: Motorcycle boots cover the leg up to above the knee to better protect the rider in a fall
zpcaka.why: Motorcycle boots protect the foot, ankle and lower leg; they do not reach above the knee.

h042m9.q: Motorcycle boots must be made entirely of fireproof rubber
h042m9.why: Motorcycle boots are not made entirely of fireproof rubber; they use tough materials such as leather with protective reinforcements.

1t9rnwt.q: There are no specific motorcycle boots, so it is best to use sturdy footwear of the type used for hunting, fishing or mountaineering
1t9rnwt.why: Specific, approved motorcycle boots do exist and are designed for riding; other footwear is not equivalent.

30aox.q: When riding mopeds or motorcycles it is advisable to wear protective gloves for the hands
30aox.why: Gloves protect the hands from impacts, abrasion and cold, and are recommended on mopeds and motorcycles.

14t63qu.q: Approved motorcyclist gloves particularly protect the back of the hand in an impact with hard objects
14t63qu.why: Approved gloves have reinforcement on the back of the hand to protect it in impacts with hard objects.

1bflcjj.q: Motorcyclist gloves protect the palm of the hand in a fall involving sliding on the asphalt
1bflcjj.why: The palm of motorcycle gloves is reinforced to withstand sliding on the asphalt.

u4qb9h.q: Motorcyclist gloves ensure proper sensitivity while riding and a more secure grip on the controls
u4qb9h.why: Motorcycle gloves are designed to keep good feel and a secure grip on the controls.

gdeikg.q: Motorcyclist gloves can have different padding depending on the season
gdeikg.why: There are lighter motorcycle gloves for summer and more heavily padded ones for winter.

deddxr.q: When riding a motorcycle, it is advisable to wear the specific gloves even in summer
deddxr.why: Gloves protect against abrasion in a fall and should be worn in summer too, in a lightweight version.

19jx1rg.q: Motorcycle gloves have special fastening systems to prevent them coming off in a fall
19jx1rg.why: Motorcycle gloves have special fastenings that stop them coming off in a fall.

rkqtol.q: There are no approved motorcycle gloves
rkqtol.why: Approved motorcycle gloves (guanti omologati) do exist and meet specific safety standards.

17v6eb1.q: Motorcycle gloves can be replaced by ski gloves, but only in the cold season
17v6eb1.why: Ski gloves lack the protection of motorcycle gloves and do not replace them in any season.

1e3e6tg.q: If you ride a motorcycle without gloves you can operate the controls more quickly
1e3e6tg.why: Without gloves you lose protection and a secure grip; you do not operate the controls any faster.

1esg595.q: Motorcycle gloves can be recognised because they are black with a motorcycle shape printed on the wrist
1esg595.why: Motorcycle gloves are recognised by their approval and protective features, not by colour or a printed motorcycle symbol.

1sb5rpy.q: Motorcycle gloves also cover the elbow to better protect in a fall
1sb5rpy.why: Motorcycle gloves protect the hand and wrist; they do not cover the elbow.

15aigi2.q: Motorcycle gloves are not suitable for riding two-wheeled mopeds
15aigi2.why: Motorcycle gloves are suitable for two-wheeled mopeds too, protecting the hands in the same way.

1h6hv8u.q: The main purpose of motorcycle gloves is to protect against the cold, so it is pointless to use them in summer
1h6hv8u.why: The main purpose of gloves is protection from impacts and abrasion, not just cold; they should be worn in summer too.

e6bpw1.q: Motorcycle jackets provide adequate protection against abrasion in a slide on the asphalt
e6bpw1.why: Motorcycle jackets are made of abrasion-resistant materials for a slide on the asphalt.

1hsw61t.q: Motorcycle jackets have rigid protective inserts at the joints
1hsw61t.why: Motorcycle jackets have rigid protectors (protezioni) at the shoulders, elbows and other joints.

1uruk08.q: Approved motorcycle clothing is subjected to cut resistance and impact abrasion tests
1uruk08.why: Approved clothing is tested for cut resistance and impact abrasion.

1dnatho.q: Approved motorcycle clothing is subjected to washing resistance tests
1dnatho.why: Approval tests cover protection in a crash, such as cut and abrasion resistance, not resistance to washing.

76mp30.q: Motorcycle jackets are not designed for summer use
76mp30.why: Summer motorcycle jackets exist, light and ventilated, and they keep the protective features.

h68yhy.q: To be approved, motorcycle jackets must be exclusively black
h68yhy.why: Approval depends on protective performance, not colour; jackets may be any colour.
